cssRecipes.name: scoped
cssRecipes.description: Documented scoped gradual-adoption recipe: the host's Bootstrap stylesheet first, then Moo UI's scoped component layer, components wrapped in .moo-ui. Chosen as the kit's canonical recipe because host conformance is about embedding Moo UI into an existing host, and this recipe exercises the @scope (.moo-ui) boundary the scoping category checks.

cssRecipes.name: full
cssRecipes.description: Documented full-replacement recipe: moo-ui.css replaces the host's Bootstrap stylesheet entirely. Recorded for contract completeness; the kit's fixtures use the scoped recipe.

categories.title: CSS reset
categories.description: Bootstrap's reboot arrives intact through the host's stylesheet pipeline, so Moo components render on the documented reset baseline.
categories.mechanism: Computed-style assertions on in-scope elements: box-sizing must be border-box on every element inside the .moo-ui wrapper (reboot universal rule), and headings inside the scope must show reboot's zeroed top margin. Pure getComputedStyle checks; no human judgment.

assertions.description: Every element inside the .moo-ui wrapper computes box-sizing to border-box.
A heading inside the .moo-ui wrapper computes margin-top to 0px, proving reboot heading normalization survived the host pipeline.

categories.title: Asset order
categories.description: The documented stylesheet cascade holds on the host: Moo UI's documented overrides win over Bootstrap defaults inside the scope, and the recipe's stylesheets are actually loaded.
categories.mechanism: Cascade-correctness outcomes are the contract, not literal request order: a host may concatenate or inline assets, so request order is only checked (and recorded as evidence) when the host serves the recipe as discrete stylesheets; an inlined or concatenated host is judged on the cascade outcome alone.

assertions.description: An in-scope .btn btn-primary computes background-color to Moo UI's foreground token (#18181b, --moo-foreground), not Bootstrap's default blue, proving Moo's layer wins the documented cascade regardless of how the host delivered it. The computed value reflects the later theme-aware button rule in moo.css, which overrides the earlier $primary-derived rule at equal specificity.

Every stylesheet named in the fixture's cssRecipe is present in the loaded document's stylesheets (matched by basename). Skipped with a recorded reason when the host concatenates or inlines styles and no discrete recipe stylesheets are observable; on such hosts moo-override-wins is the sole cascade judge, as the category mechanism states.

When the host serves the recipe as discrete stylesheet files, they are requested in the cssRecipe's documented order (bootstrap.min.css before moo.css). Skipped with a recorded reason when the host concatenates or inlines styles, since no request order exists to check there.

categories.title: Scoping
categories.description: Moo UI's scoped layer changes nothing in host content outside the .moo-ui boundary (as sampled by the documented probes) and demonstrably changes things inside it. Overlay backdrops are styled globally by design because Bootstrap teleports modals and offcanvas to the body; that is expected, not a scoping violation.
categories.mechanism: Two-pass comparison by the runner: load the fixture normally and record computed styles of out-of-scope probe elements, then reload with the moo.css stylesheet request blocked via route interception and record the same values; the two recordings must be identical for out-of-scope probes while at least one in-scope control element must differ. Hosts that concatenate Moo CSS with host styles cannot isolate the stylesheet, in which case the assertion is skipped with a recorded reason rather than forced.

assertions.description: Computed styles of host content outside the .moo-ui wrapper (heading, paragraph, link, list, plain button probes) are byte-identical across the moo.css-loaded and moo.css-blocked passes.
At least one in-scope control element's computed styles differ between the two passes, proving the block was effective and Moo's scoped layer actually applies inside .moo-ui.

categories.title: Theme
categories.description: The documented Bootstrap theme attribute switches Moo components between light and dark values inside the scope.
categories.mechanism: The runner sets data-bs-theme on the document element and re-reads computed styles of an in-scope themed surface; light and dark readings must differ and the dark reading must match Moo UI's documented dark surface token.

assertions.description: Setting data-bs-theme="dark" changes the computed background-color of the in-scope themed surface from the documented light value to the documented dark value, and removing it restores the light value.

categories.title: Direction
categories.description: Components follow the document direction: logical spacing and alignment mirror under dir="rtl".
categories.mechanism: The runner measures an asymmetric in-scope probe under dir="ltr", sets dir="rtl" on the document element, and re-measures; the probe's physical left/right spacing must swap, proving styles are written in logical properties rather than pinned physical sides.

assertions.description: An in-scope probe element with asymmetric horizontal spacing computes padding-left and padding-right swapped between dir="ltr" and dir="rtl" readings.

categories.title: Focus
categories.description: Interactive components are keyboard-reachable and show a visible focus treatment.
categories.mechanism: Playwright keyboard navigation (Tab from body) plus computed outline/box-shadow of the focused element; no human judgment of appearance, only presence of a non-none focus treatment on the focused in-scope element.

assertions.description: Pressing Tab from the document body moves focus to an interactive element inside the .moo-ui wrapper within a bounded number of Tab presses.
A keyboard-focused in-scope element computes a non-none outline-style or a non-none box-shadow, proving a visible focus treatment exists.

categories.title: Overlays
categories.description: Bootstrap-plugin-owned overlays open, layer above content, move focus where documented, and close with focus restoration.
categories.mechanism: Playwright drives the documented trigger (click or keyboard), then checks computed z-index/visibility of the overlay element, activeElement location while open, and close-and-restore behavior via Escape; all mechanical DOM and computed-style reads.

assertions.description: Activating the documented trigger makes the overlay element visible with a computed z-index at or above Bootstrap's overlay floor (1000).
While the Dialog overlay is open, document.activeElement is inside the overlay element.
Pressing Escape while the overlay is open hides it and returns focus to the original trigger element.

categories.title: Lifecycle
categories.description: Runtime ownership holds: Moo ESM components are inert until explicit initialization, initialization is idempotent and validates its root; Bootstrap Data API components work without any Moo JavaScript.
categories.mechanism: For Moo ESM fixtures the runner evaluates behavior before and after the documented getOrCreateInstance call and checks instance identity across double initialization; for the Data API fixture it verifies documented toggle behavior with only Bootstrap's bundle loaded. The pre-init state is observed with a two-pass load: the runner first loads the fixture with the external init script blocked via route interception and interacts, then reloads with it allowed; the moo-esm fixture's init script must therefore be a standalone blockable resource. All checks are scripted DOM probes; Combobox and Sidebar were confirmed to use explicit initialization with no document auto-scanning.

assertions.description: Before explicit initialization, interacting with the Combobox trigger produces no listbox (no [role=listbox] appears and aria-expanded is not true); after the fixture's initialization script runs, the same interaction opens it.
Calling getOrCreateInstance twice on the same root returns the identical instance and produces no console errors.
Constructing Sidebar against an element without the documented [data-slot=sidebar-wrapper] root throws a TypeError, proving the documented root contract is enforced.
Clicking a data-bs-toggle trigger opens its panel with only Bootstrap's JavaScript bundle loaded and no Moo ESM module on the page.

categories.title: Content Security Policy
categories.description: The kit's fixtures and Moo UI's documented runtime work under a strict CSP: no inline scripts, no inline style blocks, no eval.
categories.mechanism: Runner-side enforcement by construction: the runner intercepts responses and injects a strict Content-Security-Policy header (default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self') before collecting console messages, and the contract requires zero CSP violation reports during load and the fixture scenario. The check assumes same-origin kit assets: fixtures must reference stylesheets, scripts, and init code by relative paths, so a host deliberately serving the kit from a CDN is out of scope for this assertion by construction. Fixture initialization code must live in external script files so fixtures remain CSP-clean by construction; a static scan at fixture authoring time keeps inline handlers, style blocks, and javascript: URLs out of the fixtures.

assertions.description: With the runner-injected strict CSP header in force, the fixture produces zero CSP violation console messages and zero blocked inline executions during load and its scenario.

params.policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'

categories.title: Console health
categories.description: Fixtures load and run clean: no console errors, no uncaught exceptions, no failed resource loads.
categories.mechanism: The runner collects console messages and page errors while loading each fixture and driving its scenario, plus the network log; any error-level message, uncaught exception, or failed/blocked resource request fails the category.

assertions.description: No console.error messages and no uncaught page exceptions occur during fixture load and scenario.
Every resource the fixture requests loads successfully (no HTTP >= 400 responses, no request failures).
